title: SpaceX Stock: Why Wall Street sees more upside ahead - ​SpaceX Stock Looks to 2027 as Key Catalysts Approach | The Economic Times
text:
SpaceX is entering a potentially eventful phase as investors weigh its rocket-launch business, Starlink expansion and artificial intelligence ambitions. Upcoming milestones could influence sentiment towards the stock, making execution and growth expectations central to its outlook. (Source: Yahoo Finance, The Motley Fool)

SpaceX’s acquisition of a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio could strengthen Starlink’s wireless connectivity ambitions. The move raises the prospect of increased competition for established US telecom operators as SpaceX explores ways to expand its reach beyond satellite broadband.

SpaceX is reportedly seeking around $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia chips, highlighting the scale of its AI computing ambitions. The plan could support future growth, but investors will also assess borrowing costs, leverage and whether anticipated demand can generate sufficient returns.

Starship development remains a key factor in SpaceX's long-term investment case. Successful test flights and progress towards reusable launch systems could expand the company’s ability to deploy satellites and support future space-based computing services. Delays or technical setbacks, however, could challenge bullish expectations.

Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas has maintained a bullish stance on SpaceX, with a $300 price target in an earlier October research call. The investment thesis rests on potential growth across connectivity, launch services and AI computing. Supporters argue that stronger earnings prospects could make the valuation more attractive relative to its growth potential.

Despite its growth prospects, SpaceX faces questions over how quickly its ambitions can translate into sustainable profits. Heavy investment needs, financing risks, execution challenges and an already demanding valuation could limit returns if growth falls short of expectations. Investors will need to weigh the potential upside against the time it will take to deliver on Musk’s plans.
